title: Chicken adobo
intro: Chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar and plenty of garlic until the sauce turns glossy and clings to every piece. This is the everyday version: one pot, pantry ingredients, about an hour, and it tastes even better the next day.

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin side down in batches, about 5 minutes per batch. Set the pieces aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Fry the garlic in the chicken fat until fragrant and just turning golden. Do not let it brown.
Return the chicken to the pot with the soy sauce, water, bay leaves and peppercorns. Bring to a boil.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil without stirring, so its sharp edge cooks off.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer until the chicken is tender, turning the pieces once halfway.
Uncover, stir in the sugar if using, and simmer until the sauce has reduced by about half and coats the chicken.
Taste the sauce. Add a splash of vinegar if it needs brightness, or a splash of water if it is too salty. Remove the bay leaves.
Serve over steamed rice with plenty of sauce spooned over.

tips: Adobo keeps for 4 days in the fridge and the flavor deepens overnight. Reheat gently with a splash of water. For a crisp finish, fry the cooked pieces in a hot pan for a few minutes a side and pour the sauce over at the table.
